_note: Scene-sequential world. One speaker on stage at a time, centred and bottom-anchored. Sprites are split base + face overlay; see README.md.
name: Visual Novel

viewport._note: A constraint the runtime satisfies, never a size this world demands. Unlike Cartoon this world is genuinely fluid — every measurement in styles.css is in cqw/cqh — so it declares a RANGE rather than a single artboard aspect, per Cartoon's own _aspect_note: a world that genuinely reflows should declare none, or a range.
viewport._measured: Two things bound the range, and neither is taste. UPPER (2.10): backgrounds are 1.41-1.78 source aspect and object-fit:cover keeps bg_aspect/stage_aspect of their height — the three 1.41 backgrounds keep 79% at stage 1.78, 68% at 2.06, and 59% at 2.40. 2.10 caps the loss at 67%, which is the crop the composition was verified against. LOWER (1.78): below this the stage grows taller than the widest background, so cover starts cropping WIDTH instead and the composed edges of the art are lost. Across the three panel aspects the chrome was measured handing a world (1.96, 2.06, 2.11) this range wastes 0%, 0% and 0.5% of the panel, against 9.2%/13.6%/15.6% for a flat 1.78.
viewport._floor: The floor is the load-bearing half. Type is fixed px while the line column is 62cqw, so a narrower panel wraps the same text into more lines and the block grows into a box of fixed 27cqh. A capped 180-char line takes 3 lines at 1368 wide and clears by ~50px; at 1000 wide it takes 4 and overflows by ~20px. 1368x652 is the box this world was verified against. CAVEAT: the line-count figures assume ~0.5em per character; re-measure in a browser before trusting the exact number.

voice.person: the characters talk to each other, and to the student, who is present in the scene as a silent third classmate
voice.register: two classmates working something out. Plain, curious, a little wry.
forbidden: narration or stage directions; only spoken lines
any mention of being a model, an assistant, or generating anything
naming the speaker inside the line; the nameplate already does that
samples: So the tree stores a range in every node. That is the whole trick.
Wait. Then a query never touches more than log n of them?
That is the part everyone gets backwards, so do not feel bad about it.

line.job: One spoken line. What this character says on this beat. No quotation marks, no speaker name.

speaker_body.job: Who is speaking. Alternate between them; a stretch of the same speaker reads as a monologue.

speaker_face.job: The speaker's expression. MUST begin with the same name as speaker_body.

background.job: Where the scene takes place. Chosen once for the module.

body.mei: Mei, hime cut, brown hair, navy seifuku, round glasses. She explains and is usually right.
body.hana: Hana, twin tails, dark hair, white seifuku. She asks, guesses, and is often wrong first.

face.mei-normal: Mei: level and attentive. The default for a plain explanation.
face.mei-smile: Mei: a small closed smile, warm and unhurried.
face.mei-pleased: Mei: eyes closed, gently pleased. Use when something has just landed.
face.mei-delighted: Mei: bright and open-mouthed, genuinely excited by the idea.
face.mei-shocked: Mei: wide eyes, mouth open. Use when a result is genuinely surprising.
face.mei-sad: Mei: downcast brows, quiet. Use when an approach did not work.
face.mei-angry: Mei: brows down, mouth open. Rare, and only for a firm correction.
face.mei-smug: Mei: one brow up, a small knowing smile. Use when the answer was obvious in hindsight.
face.mei-annoyed: Mei: flat eyes, unimpressed. Use for a mistake that keeps coming back.
face.mei-sleepy: Mei: heavy lids. Use sparingly, for a long or dry stretch.
face.hana-normal: Hana: level and attentive. The default for a plain explanation.
face.hana-smile: Hana: a small closed smile, warm and unhurried.
face.hana-pleased: Hana: eyes closed, gently pleased. Use when something has just landed.
face.hana-delighted: Hana: bright and open-mouthed, genuinely excited by the idea.
face.hana-shocked: Hana: wide eyes, mouth open. Use when a result is genuinely surprising.
face.hana-sad: Hana: downcast brows, quiet. Use when an approach did not work.
face.hana-angry: Hana: brows down, mouth open. Rare, and only for a firm correction.
face.hana-smug: Hana: one brow up, a small knowing smile. Use when the answer was obvious in hindsight.
face.hana-annoyed: Hana: flat eyes, unimpressed. Use for a mistake that keeps coming back.
face.hana-sleepy: Hana: heavy lids. Use sparingly, for a long or dry stretch.

background.classroom-day: an empty classroom in daylight, desks in rows. The default setting.
background.library: a wide school library with tall windows. For research, reading, quiet work.
background.corridor-morning: a school corridor in morning light. For short scenes and asides.
background.school-gate: the school entrance, trees and open sky. For beginnings and endings.
background.basketball-court: an indoor court. For anything physical, competitive, or about movement.

motion._note: The world declares; the runtime clamps to 600ms and scales by the speed setting.

module._note: Channels belonging to the module rather than a beat. The ask screen needs one. In this world the student is a character in the scene, so a line addressed to them is in-fiction rather than a break in it.

ask_line.job: The closing line, spoken to the student after the last beat. Land what was just worked out, then ask where they want to go next. It must end in a question.
ask_line.opening: So, what are we working on today?
